kitchen-distributors.title: Kitchen Equipment for Distributors | China Sourcing | DDNZ
kitchen-distributors.description: Plan kitchen equipment for resale: compare models, order quantities, packing and spare-parts requests. Build a distributor sourcing brief with DDNZ.
kitchen-distributors.heading: Build a range your customers can buy again.
kitchen-distributors.intro: Source wholesale kitchen equipment from China for your distribution range. Bring together the equipment your customers ask for, then compare each model on the same purchasing basis. Start with a trial line, a restock or a broader assortment.
kitchen-distributors.cardCopy: Choose your first range, plan repeat orders and ask about packing and spare parts.
steps: Choose the role of each model
Separate an entry model from a larger-capacity option. For ice machines, compare rated daily output and footprint; for fryers, compare each tank. Add expected quantities before judging the price.
Compare the order behind the price

Reference prices apply to the quantity shown on the product. Ask for the same configuration, packing and delivery scope across suppliers. A mixed sourcing list still needs confirmation of each model’s minimum and availability.
Prepare for the next sale

Include manuals, carton identification and the spare parts you want quoted. Ask which parts can be ordered again and what the warranty process requires. Local installation and service arrangements belong in your own resale plan.
faqs: Can I combine ice machines, fryers and refrigeration?
Yes, you can request a mixed selection. Factory minimums, packing, consolidation and shipping are confirmed for the actual combination.
Are the displayed prices distributor quotations?
They are indicative references with their own order quantities. Your quotation confirms the selected models, quantities, currency and delivery scope.
Do I need electrical details before making the list?
Start with models, quantities and destination. We confirm voltage, frequency, phase and plug for the selected equipment during quotation.

restaurant-projects.title: Restaurant Project Equipment from China | DDNZ Global
restaurant-projects.description: Prepare an equipment sourcing brief for restaurant, café or hotel projects. Compare footprints, list quantities and confirm configurations before ordering.
restaurant-projects.heading: Turn an equipment list into a coordinated order.
restaurant-projects.intro: Source restaurant project equipment from China against your equipment schedule. Share the project, the spaces and the equipment you need. We help organize sourcing around a defined list so model choices and delivery requirements can be reviewed together.
restaurant-projects.cardCopy: Bring a project equipment list, available space and delivery requirements.
steps: Define the work each station does
Group the list into cooking, cold storage, preparation and drinks. Note what is already specified and where you need alternatives. Send equipment quantities and available counter or cabinet space.
Check the interfaces

Review overall dimensions, door clearance, ventilation, drainage and utility connections for selected models. Site suitability and installation plans should be confirmed with your project team before purchase.
Agree the order and handover scope

Include the destination, requested delivery window and any need to identify cartons by site or station. Ask which documents and packing details can accompany the shipment. Lead times and coordinated dispatch depend on the selected suppliers.
faqs: Can you quote against my existing equipment schedule?
Yes. Include model references or descriptions and quantities in the request. Mark items that are fixed and items where alternatives are welcome.
Can I request a complete kitchen installation?
This page covers equipment sourcing and export coordination. Tell us any installation needs so responsibilities can be clarified in the quotation; local installation is not included by default.
What if the opening date is already fixed?
Include your requested date and destination. Production, consolidation, transit and local delivery need to be checked before a delivery commitment is made.

phone-stores.title: Wholesale Screen Protectors for Stores & Chains | DDNZ
phone-stores.description: Plan screen protectors for accessory stores and repair chains. Compare phone-model minimums, installation kits and packing before requesting a bulk order.
phone-stores.heading: Plan the phone mix before you place the order.
phone-stores.intro: Buy wholesale screen protectors from China for phone stores and repair chains. Build a replenishment list around the phones your stores actually serve. Compare clear and privacy options, installation methods and quantities per phone model.
phone-stores.cardCopy: Plan model coverage, installation and repeat orders across your stores.
steps: Write down the exact phone models

Include the phone name and generation, then assign a quantity to each protector and phone combination. Avoid treating all variants of one phone series as the same fit. The existing product minimums still apply.
Match the protector to the sale

Compare a privacy option with a clear option and decide whether store staff or the customer will install it. Confirm the installer, cleaning accessories and retail package against the selected product.
Plan stock by store or central warehouse

Tell us how you want the shipment allocated. Carton quantities, mixed-model packing and store labels need to be checked before dispatch. Keep a confirmed sample and model list for your next replenishment.
faqs: Can several stores share one order?
You can submit a combined request. Product and phone-model minimums still apply; store allocation and packing are confirmed with the quotation.
Can I assume every phone model is available?
No. The exact phone-model list, fit and availability must be confirmed for the products you choose.
Do the prices include shipping to my country?
Product references do not include a destination quotation. State your country and quantities. The separate English freight calculator uses an Istanbul reference only.

private-label.title: Private Label Screen Protector Sourcing | DDNZ Global
private-label.description: Request screen protectors for your own brand. Define glass, installation kits, packaging, phone models and sample checks before a private label quotation.
private-label.heading: Build the product behind your brand.
private-label.intro: Source private-label screen protectors from China with product and packaging specifications for your brand. Use the current screen-protector range as a starting point. Describe the product, packaging and customer experience you want, then request a supplier review of the changes.
private-label.cardCopy: Define the protector, installation kit and packaging you want quoted.
steps: Specify the product first

Choose clear or privacy glass, the intended phone models and the installation format. Use samples to review fit, edge coverage, touch response and case compatibility before approving a production specification.
Separate product and packaging changes

Describe whether you need a label, printed retail box, instructions or a different accessory set. Branding availability, artwork requirements, setup charges and minimums are confirmed by the selected supplier.
Approve a repeatable specification

Agree the sample, artwork version, packing list and inspection points. List any barcode or channel-label requirements you need reviewed. Approval for a particular sales platform is not implied by a packaging request.
faqs: Is custom packaging already included in the reference price?
No. The displayed product references cover the described options. Any custom packaging, printing or tooling requires a separate confirmed quotation.
Is there a fixed private-label minimum order?
Custom requirements may change minimum quantities. Share the quantity by phone model and the packaging changes so the supplier can review them.
Can I request a sample before a bulk order?
Yes. Ask for the sample configuration, cost and delivery arrangement. Confirm it against your intended phone models and packaging before approving a larger order.
